what: The trace along Henon's family m (Celestial Mechanics 13 (1976) 267, Table I) made with the ias route from his orbit 5, and its comparison with his table. Equal masses, the perpendicular start of src/perp.js: u1, u2, lam, t as everywhere (t half the period). Henon's values are the ones printed in his Table I (8 decimals), typed from a scan and checked by his energy E = -1/6 and by A; five of the 45 rows (orbits 2, 3, 4, 6, 11) do not pass the energy check at 1e-7 (the printed digits give 1e-7 to 5e-7 at their small pair distances) and are not used as values (orbit 11 is compared by its lam, the zero of the rotation angle). His rows are converted to our units (masses 1, G = 1, energy -1/2 scaled to the start x = -1, lam, 1 of src/perp.js) with the steps of the conversion given in the field conversion.
conversion: time unit and velocity unit: s = 2 / (x_r - x_l); lam = -1 + 2 (x_m - x_l) / (x_r - x_l); u1 = sqrt(3) s^(-1/2) v_l, u2 = sqrt(3) s^(-1/2) v_m, t = (T / 2) s^(3/2) / sqrt(3), where x_l, x_m, x_r and v_l, v_m are the printed positions and velocities of the left, middle and right body at the start of the half period and T is his period.
corrector: the bound on t in the line search of the corrector (src/shooting.js) is relative to the predicted point, 0.3 * t < t_trial < 3 * t; before that it was relative to the t of the start of the run, and the same run stopped at lam 0.6680289 (step 223, t = 0.38965 = 0.3 * 1.29885)
commands: python tools/reclose.py JOB.json OUT.json    (50 digits; the job holds u1, u2, t from the cubic through the four recorded points nearest in lam at the lam of Henon's orbit and ref = his converted values)
node test/t-bound.test.js    (the first 90 seconds of the same run in one process)

stop.why: the driver ended with an error in relativeStability (src/relative.js, called by the driver for every recorded point): "eigenvalue iteration did not converge" in the eigenvalues of src/stability.js at the accepted step 456, after the recorded point of step 455 (lam 0.9957458, t 0.00062, closest approach 0.0043, L* 17.2). The points below are those recorded before the error. Henon's table ends at orbit 46 (lam 0.9437) and the end row (A to infinity, lam to 1).

orbit_11.how: lam of the zero of the rotation angle theta, found and refined by huntArclength (all: true, the zero refined along the family) in the run of test/t-bound.test.js; the cubic through the four recorded points nearest in lam (inverse interpolation, steps used) is given for comparison and is only as good as the spacing of the recorded points there (0.03 in lam)
